props.gloss_en: Rav Yehuda: three things, whoever prolongs them has his days and years prolonged -- one who prolongs his prayer
and one who prolongs [his time] at his table
and one who prolongs [his time] in the privy
R' Yochanan: whoever prolongs his prayer and looks into it ends in heartache
as it is said: 'hope deferred makes the heart sick' (Prov 13:12)
R' Yitzchak: three things recall a person's sins -- a leaning wall
and looking into prayer [recalls a person's sins]
and handing over judgment against one's fellow to Heaven [recalls a person's sins]
no difficulty: this [R' Yochanan's heartache] where he looks into it
that [Rav Yehuda's lengthened days] where he does not look into it
and how does he do it? he multiplies supplication
and one who prolongs at his table: perhaps a poor man will come and he will give him [food]

as it is written: 'the altar of wood, three cubits high', and it is written: 'and he said to me, this is the table that is before the Lord' (Ezek 41:22) -- it opened with the altar and closed with the table!
R' Yochanan and R' Elazar: as long as the Temple stood, the altar atoned for Israel
and now, a person's table atones for him

ten things bring a person to hemorrhoids: eating reed leaves, vine leaves, vine tendrils, an animal's palate, a fish's spine, salted fish not fully cooked; drinking wine lees; wiping with lime or clay; wiping with a pebble another has wiped with
some say: also one who strains himself in the privy too much [is brought to hemorrhoids]
no difficulty: this [the baraita] where he prolongs and strains
that [Rav Yehuda's lengthened days] where he prolongs and does not strain
the matron to R' Yehuda b'R' Ilai: your face is like those of pig-breeders and usurers
R' Yehuda b'R' Ilai: truly, both are forbidden to me; rather, there are twenty-four privies from my lodging to the study hall, and when I go I check myself in all of them
Rav Yehuda: three things shorten a person's days and years -- one who is given a Torah scroll to read and does not read
[one given] a cup of blessing to bless and does not bless
and one who conducts himself with lordliness
a Torah scroll to read and he does not read: as it is written, 'for it is your life and the length of your days' (Deut 30:20)
a cup of blessing to bless and he does not bless: as it is written, 'and I will bless those who bless you' (Gen 12:3)
R' Chama b'R' Chanina: why did Joseph die before his brothers? because he conducted himself with lordliness
